event.title: Nordic Book Circle
event.description:
Contemporary Nordic literature is full of diverse literary voices, styles, and genres. This September 2026 through May 2027 the ASI Nordic Book Circle will gather monthly, in-person, to read and discuss a work of Nordic literature in English translation. Our focus this year will be on works of literature written by women authors from across the Nordic world. The works we read will chronologically trace books penned between 1912 and 2020, and include two winners of the Nobel Prize in Literature; authors from the countries of Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Iceland, Greenland; various genres; and a range of topics and perspectives. If you love to read and discuss literature and would like to expand your appreciation of literature from various parts of the world (the Nordic world in particular), we would love to have you join! Limited to 20 attendees; please register in advance.

2026-2027 Nordic Book Circle titles
September: Kristin Lavransdotter, Book I: The Wreath (1912), by Sigrid Undset, translated from Norwegian by Tiina Nunnally (Penguin Editions, 336 pages), Norway – September 27, 2026

October: The Phantom Carriage (1912), by Selma Lagerlöf, translated from Swedish by Peter Graves (Norvik Press, 124 pages) (Sweden) – October 25, 2026

November: Quicksand (1928) by Nella Larsen (Penguin Classics, 192 pages) (Denmark) – November 22, 2026

December: Kallocain (1940), Karin Boye, translated from Swedish by David McDuff (Penguin Classics, 192 pages) (Sweden) – December 20, 2026

January: Girl Upon Heaven’s Pier (1951), by Eeva-Liisa Manner, translated from Finnish by Terhi Kuusisto (Dalkey Archive Press, 104 pages) (Finland) – January 31, 2027

February: Nothing to be Rescued (1961), by Ásta Sigurðardóttir, translated from Icelandic by Meg Matich (Nordisk Books, 192 pages) Iceland – February 28, 2027

March: Light, Grass, and Letter in April (1962, 1963, 1979), by Inger Christensen, translated from Danish by Susanna Nied (New Directions Publishing, 144 pages) (Denmark) – March 21, 2027

April: Zombieland (2015), by Sørine Steenholdt, translated from Greenlandic to Danish by Niviaq Korneliussen and from Danish to English by Charlotte Barslund (Norvik Press, 150 pages) (Greenland) – April 25, 2027

May: Strega (2020), by Johanna Lykke Holm, translated from Swedish by Saskia Vogel (Riverhead Books, 208 pages) (Sweden) – May 23, 2027

Performance Club is a FREE opportunity to showcase your works-in-progress, develop confidence in performance, and try a new skill in front of supportive peers and an Artist-Faculty leader from Omaha Conservatory of Music. event.title: Battlefield Memorial March 2026
event.description:
As part of the nationwide America 250 commemoration, Coastal Heritage Society invites the community to honor those who fought in the 1779 Battle of Savannah, one of the Revolutionary War’s most pivotal conflicts, where approximately 800 troops were killed or wounded.

It is our privilege each year to remember their sacrifice and reflect on Savannah’s enduring role in our nation’s founding.

This event is free and open to the public.

Click Here to RSVP!

Battlefield Memorial March will lead guests through the footsteps of soldiers on that historic day in 1779. The march will begin at 9:00 am. All march participants will meet in the Savannah History Museum parking lot at 8:45 am.

After the march, a wreath-laying and remembrance ceremony will be held on Battlefield Memorial Park.

This remembrance event welcomes over 150 community members, elected officials, foreign dignitaries, and descendants of those who fought.

New this year: Sponsorship opportunities are available starting at $1,000.

Support Battlefield Memorial March

Title Sponsor – $5,000

  • Recognition in event remarks
  • All recognition benefits listed below

Event Sponsor – $2,500

  • Recognition in press release
  • Sponsorship acknowledgement post on social media
  • All recognition benefits listed below

Patron – $1,000

  • Logo placement in direct emails to over 6,500+ households
  • Logo placement on event landing page
  • Logo placement on event signage

Please email development@chsgeorgia.org to learn more or sponsor the march.

We hope to see you on October 9th for Battlefield Memorial March 2026.

Pin Point Heritage Museum is open from Thursday – Saturday from 9am to 4pm.

Located in the former A.S. Varn & Son Oyster and Crab Factory, guests can discover the Gullah/Geechee culture and unique lifeways, from daily life to religion, language, and food directly from residents who grew up in the small, close-knit community.

event.title: OFJ: Daily Programming and Cannon Firings
event.description: Join us for family-friendly educational programming focusing on the lives of soldiers once stationed at Fort Jackson and its 18th-century predecessor, Mud Fort! CHS Historical Interpreters will lead interactive programs on weaponry, wartime communications, military medicine, and more, while dressed as soldiers from different units present on-site over the 250 years of its history.

event.title: HFH Closed
event.description:
Harper Fowlkes House is closed on Saturday, October 17, for a private event.

Regular hours: Open Mondays, Wednesdays, and Saturdays from 10:00am-3:00pm with the last guided tour at 2:00pm.

Visitors can learn about the unique features and history of the Harper Fowlkes House and tour the beautiful garden.

TICKETS ON SALE NOW: Click Here

Frogwarts: A Magical Adventure! returns Sunday, October 25th, 2026, to Georgia State Railroad Museum and Savannah Children’s Museum.

Coastal Heritage Society’s signature fall family fundraiser is a wizarding-themed day filled with train rides, STEAM activities, wand making, potions, reptiles, owls, food trucks, and more magical fun!

Please note: 

  • A train ride is included in the price of admission, unless an Activities Only Ticket is purchased.
  • The museums will be closed from 9 to 11 a.m. for event set up.
  • Guests are encouraged to arrive early for their train ride.
  • Activities run 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., so arrive any time BEFORE your scheduled train ride time!

Thank you to our generous event sponsors:

If you are interested in supporting Frogwarts 2026, please contact us at development@chsgeorgia.org.
